chapter_theme: The eight-petalled lotus and the states of the three gunas: the eight directions with their guardian gods are set as the petals of an inner lotus, through whose stalk the sushumna rises to a light; the Lord stands in the eight, in the grades beyond them and in the ages, and is reached at the summit, where a tank fills without a river and a lotus blooms without mud.
structure_note: 2527 and 2531 name the eight directions and their gods; 2528 and 2529 make them the petals of the inner lotus; 2532 to 2534 rank the grades beyond the eight and the ages; 2530 and 2535 give the tank and lotus at the summit; 2536 closes with those who seek him. The three gunas of the title are named in no verse.

2527.reading: Indra in the east where the sun rises, Agni, Yama, the praised Nirriti, Varuna, good Vayu, honoured Kubera and Isana of the north stand filling the eight directions.
2527.nuance: The list is the standard eight guardians of the quarters, in order round the compass. Placed here, they are traditionally read as presiding over the eight petals of the heart lotus. நிதித்து (keeping guard?) is unclear.

2528.reading: The gathered flower has eight petals, and close within it is the city of maya; through the sushumna inside the narrowed stalk, perceive the gathered light and rise, and be saved.
2528.nuance: The eight-petalled lotus is traditionally placed at the heart; தண்டு (stalk) is the spinal column and சுழுனை the central channel. மாயாபுரி (city of maya) may be the body or the lotus itself.

2529.reading: There are three lotuses in bud, and in all three the light, a spreading flame, opens them; if one enters two petals within the eight, an old thing blooms and is a dream.
2529.nuance: The three lotuses may be the three gunas or three centres; the title suggests the gunas. The last line seems to tie entering two of the petals to the dream state, but what பண்டம் (old thing) is cannot be fixed.

2530.reading: There is a river, and a tank within; Siva's way is a hundred, its colour subtle; the precious Thing stays apart, with her of full breasts as his share.
2530.nuance: The river and inner tank are read as the flow of nectar to a reservoir in the head, as in 2535. நூறே (a hundred) and கொண்பனையாள் are obscure. கூறு (share) recalls Shakti as half of Siva's body, yet he is said to stay apart (வேறே).

2531.reading: The first Lord, who stands as the eight directions, the eight chariots, the eight deities and the eight kinds, fills there the eight and the four, and this is how he rises within the eight buds.
2531.nuance: The verse multiplies eights to place the Lord in every petal. தேர் எட்டும் (eight chariots) and வகை எட்டு நான்கும் (eight and four, or eight fours) are unclear.

2532.reading: Seven are with form; passing what is spoken, in the eighth lives the Supreme; passing that, in the ninth the Parapara of the ages; in the high tenth, the lone nature that descends as the sky.
2532.nuance: சகளம் (with parts, with form) set against higher, formless grades is Siddhanta language, but which seven, and what the eighth to tenth are, the verse does not say. தாழ்வது வான may also be read 'that is lower than the sky' or 'that bows'.

2533.reading: The one of many ages, the sun, the Lord; the ages within the five good ages, the age that passes into the cosmos; in that age, at its summit, in the One, is Bhagavan.
2533.nuance: ஊழி (aeon) repeats in every line. The five ages may be cosmic cycles or the five states; the summit of the age may be the end of dissolution or the top of the head. The reading is a guess.

2534.reading: The eight elephants that bear the world, the roaming tusker with the throngs of gods, fire, rain and the moving air all have their hold in the vast space.
2534.nuance: The eight elephants are those of the quarters, and the tusker Indra's Airavata. பரியும் ஆகாசம் may be the vast space or the space that bears; tradition may read it as the inner space where the Lord is.

2535.reading: On the summit of a high hill where springs rise there is a rare tank that fills without a river; the one with twisted locks wears the rich lotus that bloomed without mud, without a flower.
2535.nuance: Each line holds a paradox: a tank with no river, a lotus with no mud, a flower worn with no flower. The hill is commonly the head, the tank the nectar there and the lotus the thousand-petalled one; plainly, the verse says the Lord's things need none of the world's causes.

2536.reading: When one and two have joined, though people stand and sit and talk of many lands, those who conquer and stay seeking the changeless one, going or staying, are the ones who reach the sacred.
2536.nuance: ஒன்றும் இரண்டும் (one and two) may be the soul with Siva and Shakti, or the breath and mind, or the two side channels with the central one. திருவடையோர் may be 'those who reach the sacred' or 'those who reach the holy feet'.

links.note: 2530 names a river and an inner tank; 2535 places the tank on a hilltop, filled without a river, and adds the lotus without mud worn by Siva.
Both set standing and sitting and many words against the one who conquers and seeks the Lord: talk and posture do not reach him, mastery does.

source_issues: The chapter title names the three gunas, but no verse in the chapter names them.
2527 line 4: நிதித்தெண் டிசையு is unclear, perhaps for நிதித்து எண்டிசையும்.
2533 line 3: அண்டத்துக் சென்ற is a misprint for அண்டத்துச் சென்ற.
2530 line 3: கொண்பனை யாள் is obscure and may be corrupt.
